- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.8) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce overshoot by 10–15% to avoid overcorrection.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.2) and forecast is falling, avoid excessive downward bias — add 5–10% to prevent premature bottoming.  
- After a recent spike in price, model tends to overreact — apply a 10–15% downward correction in the next 3–5 days.  
- Mean reversion is stronger in low-sentiment periods — if sentiment <0.4, apply a 5–10% upward bias toward historical mean over 10-day window.  
- Forecast horizon 30d is prone to lagging sentiment shifts — if sentiment turns positive within 5 days, adjust forecast to reflect 2–3 day lag effect.  
- Avoid forecasting below 65% of recent 10-day low if sentiment is neutral or negative — this triggers underestimation bias.
